items.text: The environment in which a plant lives. <break time="0.8s" /> Is inseparable from the plant itself. <break time="0.8s" /> The environment informs. <break time="0.8s" /> What kind of plant the offspring will become. <break time="0.8s" /> The kind that survives and thrives. <break time="0.8s" /> In a challenging scenario. <break time="0.8s" /> Or does not. <break time="0.8s" /> It changes plants body plan. <break time="0.8s" /> And possibly directs their development. <break time="0.8s" /> And those changes can be passed down. <break time="0.8s" /> To their offspring. <break time="0.8s" /> Whose body will develop differently from the start. <break time="0.8s" /> And be better able to handle. <break time="0.8s" /> The harsh conditions its parents experienced. <break time="0.8s" /> In other words. <break time="0.8s" /> Parent plants can pass on. <break time="0.8s" /> Skills for surviving in a tough world. <break time="0.8s" /> In some cases. <break time="0.8s" /> This involves whole new body parts. <break time="0.8s" /> And coats of armor. <break time="0.8s" /> For example. <break time="0.8s" /> Wild radishes that have lived through an attack of destructive caterpillars. <break time="0.8s" /> Will make baby radishes with extra scratchy leaves. <break time="0.8s" /> And they will be preloaded with defensive chemicals. <break time="0.8s" /> To better keep away threats. <break time="0.8s" /> If these plant children end up facing. <break time="0.8s" /> The same challenges their parents did. <break time="0.8s" /> They will be much better prepared. <break time="0.8s" /> To handle them.
